name: Mend the Beast
gloss: Close a working animal's injury before the season is lost along with it. Unglamorous, and the reason the ox that hauls stone for a library is usually the same ox for thirty years.

name: Quicken the Herd
gloss: Bring a herd into season early and see it take. The primitive it moves is the same one that counts student intakes, which the faculty of medicine finds vulgar and the bursar does not.

name: Call the Pack
gloss: Make beasts, whole and willing, out of the material of the place. They are honest animals and behave like it, which is the standing complaint of everyone who has tried to use them as soldiers.

name: The Fat Year
gloss: Hold a whole countryside in abundance for a year. Towns that eat well raise more children, and the university finds out twenty years later, in the size of one entering class.

name: The Made Beast
gloss: Conjure a creature that never existed, and discover that it breeds true. The practical literature is four pages; the literature on whether one may is a shelf.

name: Draw the Sweet Water
gloss: Make clean water where the ground offers none. A siege is arithmetic about wells, and this working changes the arithmetic.

name: The Unfailing Well
gloss: A well that does not go down in a dry year. Cheap to hold, and impossible to explain to a neighbouring town whose well does.

name: Turn the Channel
gloss: Put a river where the mills and the fields want it. Everything downstream of the old course becomes a matter for the courts, and the courts have been busy since the working was first published.

name: Raise the River
gloss: Raise water out of nothing at the volume of a river, and keep raising it. The same working supplies a city and drowns a besieging camp; the treatises differ only on which use to describe first.

name: Turn the Wind
gloss: Put the wind where a mill or a drying floor wants it. The most-cast working in any university that owns farmland, and the least written about.

name: Clear the Sky
gloss: Hold weather off a place for a day. Harvest and roof-work want the same day, and a university that can promise one is immediately asked for the other.

name: Call the Storm
gloss: Evocation as the older texts meant it: weather made, aimed, and left running over a field somebody else is standing in. It is not a stronger working than the one that saves a harvest. It is that working, pointed.

name: The Borrowed Season
gloss: Keep a growing season open past the month it should have closed. Universities that hold it eat in years their neighbours do not, which has done more for enrolment than any prospectus.

name: Keep the Sky
gloss: Hold a climate over one valley indefinitely. The neighbouring valleys receive whatever is left over, and there is a long body of law about that.

name: Close the Wound
gloss: Knit a body back to the shape it held an hour ago. Over a career an infirmary staffed by one such mage is worth about two years to everyone who passes through it, which is the first number anyone in the discipline learns to quote.

name: The Mended Decade
gloss: Correct the slow failures rather than the fast ones. A physician-mage on the faculty adds most of a decade to everyone else on it, and does it quietly enough that the endowment is always the last to notice.

name: Quicken the Cohort
gloss: Carry a difficult birth through, at the scale of a whole population rather than a bedside. The slowest lever a god holds and the only one that compounds: a larger entering class is a larger faculty in forty years.

name: The Long Tenure
gloss: Twenty more years of working life for everyone who holds it. It sits at tier 3 deliberately, so that orcs — depth ceiling 3, and the shortest-lived of the six — can reach the one working that answers what is actually wrong with them.

name: The Unfinished Death
gloss: Hold one scholar at the point where the body has finished and the work has not. The cap is half a species' natural span, so this exhausts it for a human and is a rounding error for a dragon. The objection is not that it fails; it is that the chair has not been vacated in ninety years.

name: Make the Small Luck
gloss: Fortune, made in quantities too small to prove. The literature on whether it works at all is the largest in the discipline and the least conclusive.

name: The Promised Year
gloss: Make a promise about a year and let the year arrange itself around it. A god whose scholars can do this is asked for fewer miracles and given more.

name: The Fated Hand
gloss: A mage who cannot be struck is not shielded. The arrow turns out to have been aimed somewhere else the whole time, and the archer will say so under oath.

name: Write the Ending
gloss: Fix how a thing ends and let the middle find its own way there. Nothing survives between the third tier of this cell and this one: either the intervening work was never done, or it was done and is in no catalogue.

name: The Given Destiny
gloss: Give a person a fate they did not have. Every surviving instruction opens with the same warning: the caster becomes part of the fate and cannot be written out of it afterwards. Only the two deepest species can hold it at all.

name: Quicken the Seed
gloss: Bring a crop up in the time it takes to walk the field. The yield is unchanged; what changes is how many times in a year the field is a field.

name: Grow the Beam
gloss: Grow a beam already in the shape the roof wants it, joint and curve together. Carpenters who learn what it does to their trade tend to learn the working.

name: Paper Without Rags
gloss: Grow paper rather than beat it out of rags. A university that grows its own paper writes several times more of it, and nobody has proposed a mechanism for that other than cost.

name: The Grown Hall
gloss: Grow a building instead of raising one. It takes a decade and cannot be hurried past its own season, which is why the cloisters of the older universities are all exactly the same age.

name: Strike the Light
gloss: A flame that needs no fuel and does not go out when the window is open. The first working most universities teach, because a lamp that costs nothing buys more reading hours than any endowment.

name: Hold the Temperature
gloss: Keep a kiln, a forge, or a crucible at exactly one heat for as long as the work takes. Fire's entire practical literature is about holding a number still, and none of it is about throwing anything.

name: The Assayer's Flame
gloss: A flame pure enough that what it burns can be read off its colour. Half the metallurgy in the archive is downstream of one lamp and a patient afternoon.

name: The Uncontained Hour
gloss: The kiln working with the restraint taken out. It is not a separate discovery, and the literature is embarrassed about that; it is also why a fire licence is countersigned by the treasurer rather than the dean.

name: The Standing Furnace
gloss: A fire that feeds itself and stays where it was put. It runs the great foundries, and it denies a field to anyone who would rather not walk through a foundry.

name: Cast the Likeness
gloss: Make an image that holds still and can be walked around. The illustrated lecture, arriving centuries before cheap paper; students who have seen a thing argue about it less.

name: The Shown Interior
gloss: Show the inside of a thing without opening the thing. Anatomy, siege engines, and the workings of a lock are all taught this way, and the last of those has been raised in council more than once.

name: The Absent Scholar
gloss: Leave your likeness at the desk and be elsewhere. The standard alibi, and the standard reason a disciplinary board stopped accepting one.

name: The Crowded Hall
gloss: Fill a courtyard with people who are not there. Illusion's one honest combat use: the arrows spent on them are real, and eight is the most that will ever stand, because the ninth is always the one that gets noticed.

name: The Perfect Forgery
gloss: An image of a grimoire, accurate down to the name on every page. It reads correctly and teaches correctly, and it stops doing either on the day the mage who cast it dies — which no catalogue records.

name: Set the Doorstep
gloss: Make a threshold where the architecture provided none. A line across a floor that behaves, from then on, like a wall's business.

name: Draw the Circle
gloss: The scholar's circle, made rather than drawn: a boundary that holds because it is one, and not because chalk is persuasive.

name: The Made Door
gloss: Put a door in a wall that had none, and a corridor behind it the building did not have room for. Declares no portal effect and never will: making a threshold is not opening one, and the raid gate stays in Rego Limen (contracts.md §8).

name: The Threshold That Was Always There
gloss: Make a seam, then make it old, so that the record agrees it was always a seam. Intellego Limen reads it as genuine, which is the entire point and the reason several universities decline to teach it.

name: Kindle the Question
gloss: Put a question into a mind that was not asking one. Tutors call it cheating, and use it in the first week of every term.

name: The Given Memory
gloss: Make a memory of a lesson that was never sat through. It is indistinguishable from having learned the thing, which is the entire content of the objection to it.

name: The Second Attention
gloss: Make a scholar a second attention to think with, running alongside the first. It costs nothing she notices until she is sixty, and then it costs all of it at once.

name: The Made Scholar
gloss: A mind with no body, kept in a room, that reads. The oldest of them are older than the universities built around them, and none of them will say so.

name: Give the Use-Name
gloss: Attach a name to a thing that had none, and have it stick. A catalogue is impossible before this working and merely tedious after it.

name: Name the Unnamed
gloss: Make a true name for something that has never had one — a new working, a made beast, a hall that was grown rather than built. The name is correct, which is not the same as it being deserved.

name: The Name That Teaches
gloss: Build a name so that holding it conveys the thing named. In a True Naming universe this is a term's curriculum in one syllable, and it is why those universities' terms are shorter.

name: The Second Name
gloss: Make yourself a second true name, so that the first can be spent. Perdo Nomen can take a name away; this puts a spare on the shelf, and a mage holding both is difficult to end and impossible to cite.

name: Make the Brick
gloss: Stone out of nothing, one brick at a time, at a price in mage-months no quarry would survive being compared to. The point is not the brick; it is that the brick appears where no cart can go.

name: The Poured Wall
gloss: Make a wall as a single piece, with no courses for anything to fail along. Perdo Terram takes considerably longer with these, which is the argument that gets them funded.

name: The Conjured Vein
gloss: Make ore in the ground, in the shape ore takes, where a survey would expect to find it. Three universities' worth of argument exists on whether conjured silver is silver; the mints hold their own view.

name: The Raised Bastion
gloss: Raise a fortification in an afternoon, out of material that was not there in the morning. Every siege doctrine written before the working assumes a wall takes a season, and all of them are still on the syllabus.

name: Cast the Shadow
gloss: Make a shadow where nothing stands to cast one. Trivial, and the first half of everything else in the form.

name: The Lengthened Dusk
gloss: Hold the hour after sunset over a place for as long as attention lasts. Guards keep the watch they were rostered for and not the one the light says they should.

name: The Kept Shadow
gloss: Put a thing into a shadow and take it out again later. A library kept this way cannot be burned and can be lost by forgetting which wall it was cast on; the Art of Memory faculty consider the whole approach plagiarism.

name: The Unlit Hall
gloss: Take a building out of the light entirely. Raiding parties have crossed the courtyard, emptied the wrong hall, and left with the library standing behind them.

name: Kindle the Aura
gloss: Thicken the magic of a place the way one banks a fire. Everything cast in the room afterwards is easier, and nobody can say by how much without casting it twice.

name: Feed the Working
gloss: Pour raw magic into a working that is already running, including somebody else's. The etiquette around doing this uninvited is older than most of the universities that teach it.

name: The Standing Aura
gloss: Make a place permanently easier to work in. This is why universities sit where they sit, and why the ones that were sited for the river have all quietly moved.

name: The Warded Precinct
gloss: Make enough raw magic in one place that it stands between what is cast at the precinct and the precinct. Nothing about it is clever: it is a wall built out of the same stuff as the arrow.

name: The Made Vis
gloss: Magic made rather than gathered. Every economy in the multiverse is priced on the assumption that this is impossible, and the four universities that hold it have each independently decided not to publish.

name: Cut the Sign
gloss: Take an hour-old print for everything it is: what made it, what weight it was carrying, and whether it was hurrying away from something that is still nearby.

name: Number the Herd
gloss: Know how many, of what ages, and which of them will not see the winter — without penning a single animal to be looked at. Herders who have it stop losing the whole beast to find out it was sick.

name: Chart the Migration
gloss: Know where the herds will be a season before the herds have decided. The first working in this cell that pays for a granary rather than a supper.

name: The Beast's Own Eye
gloss: Borrow what an animal is looking at, from wherever it happens to be standing. A scholar whose watchmen are all crows is difficult to surprise, and impossible to catch listening — nothing she posted can be questioned afterwards.

name: Sound the Well
gloss: Find how deep the water truly sits, and whether it will still be sitting there in August, without lowering a rope into it.

name: Sip the Standing Pool
gloss: Learn what is in a water before drinking enough of it to learn the ordinary way. Whole siege years turn on which of a city's three cisterns is the one that kills.

name: Trace the Current
gloss: Follow a moving water back to where it comes from and forward to where it means to go, including the stretches of it that are underground and the stretches that are somebody else's.

name: Fathom the Watershed
gloss: Hold every water of a country in one perception at once — springs, seeps, the river's bad years, the marsh that used to be a lake. Mills get sited on this, and so do the arguments about who owns the rain.

name: The Ache Before Rain
gloss: The old soldier's knee, made deliberate and made accurate. Three days' warning saves more harvests than any working of Creo, and costs a university nothing to keep.

name: Gauge the Wind's Road
gloss: Perceive the wind aloft, which is not the wind you are standing in and rarely agrees with it. Everything that sails or grinds is scheduled against this.

name: Reckon the Season
gloss: Take a whole year's weather in advance, coarsely, and be right about it more often than not. Coarse and usually right is worth more to a granary than precise and occasional.

name: The Lightning's Chosen Ground
gloss: Know which stone the storm has already picked, and put the library on a different one. Universities that hold this working lose towers at a rate their neighbours find suspicious.

name: Take the Pulse
gloss: Two fingers at a wrist, and the whole of what the body is currently doing about itself. Every physician thinks she can already do this; the ones who can are the ones who stop being surprised.

name: Sift the Humours
gloss: Separate what is wrong with a body from what is merely unusual about it. The great saving is not in the cures it enables but in the ones it stops a physician from attempting.

name: Listen at the Ribs
gloss: Attend to the sounds a body makes only on the inside, and know which of them is new. Everything worth catching is quiet for a year first.

name: Tell the Hour of a Body
gloss: Say how long this body has, from the body alone. It is not fate — Fatum reads the hour that was appointed; this reads only the hour the flesh is already walking toward, which is why it can be argued with.

name: Cast the Lots
gloss: The oldest divination there is, made honest. The lots were always random; this working is the part that makes them not, and every student's first result is indistinguishable from luck.

name: The Omen and the Coincidence
gloss: Separate the sign that means something from the enormous number of things that merely happened. This is the entire discipline, and the reason Fatum scholars are so tiresome about method.

name: The Fork Seen From Above
gloss: Stand outside a decision and see both roads to their ends at once. Applied to research it says which line of enquiry pays; applied to a student it says which one is worth the hours, which is the part the faculty argues about.

name: The Appointed Hour
gloss: Know the hour the world has set aside for you. It does not move. But a scholar who knows which afternoon to spend indoors buys back all the years that were never appointed at all, and most deaths were never appointed.

name: The Thread Fate Set Down
gloss: Perceive your own thread so exactly that you can tell the moment fate puts it down to attend to someone else — and live in those moments. Nothing that works by destiny can find a mage who is not currently being tracked by it. Archmages who hold it tend to have no recorded death.

name: Sight the Blight
gloss: See the rot in a field on the morning it decides to happen, rather than on the morning it shows.

name: Question the Orchard
gloss: Put the question to the trees themselves — what they are short of, what they are hoarding, which of them is dying quietly and taking the row with it.

name: Pick Out the Simple
gloss: Know a medicinal herb by its leaf, its hour, and its ground, and know it apart from the four things in the same hedge that will kill the patient instead. Most of herb-lore is the apart-from.

name: The Root Beneath the Root
gloss: Perceive the thing a forest is doing under the soil, where it is not a thousand trees but one argument. Foresters who learn it stop calling the wood a crop, which their treasurers dislike.

name: Judge the Kiln
gloss: Know the state of a fire without opening the door to it, which is the only way to know the state of a fire.

name: The Colour of Ready Iron
gloss: Smiths have always read heat by colour and always argued about it. This settles the argument, and a smithy that stops arguing produces roughly a third more.

name: Scry the Coals
gloss: The old fire-gazing, done properly. What returns is not a picture but a pressure, and the discipline is entirely in refusing to improve it into a picture on the way to the page.

name: Where the Fire Will Go
gloss: Perceive a fire's whole future path through a building before it has taken the first yard of it. Fire-wardens use it to choose what to wet; the other profession that wants it uses it to choose what not to.

name: Catch the Painted Thing
gloss: Notice that what you are looking at is a picture of itself. The first lesson is that the tell is never in the image; it is in how little the image is bothering to be looked at from the side.

name: Watch the Light Lie
gloss: Attend to the mechanism of a false image rather than to the image. Knowing exactly how a thing is not seen is the first half of not being seen, and this cell reaches concealment from that side rather than from hiding.

name: The Room You Are Not In
gloss: Take the sight and sound of a place you are nowhere near, entire, without sending anything there to fetch it. Every treaty on scrying is really about this working, and none of them has ever been enforceable.

name: Nothing Painted Passes
gloss: No false image within reach survives being looked at. The same perception run backwards tells the mage precisely where the looking in a room is going, and she is never standing there.

name: Sense the Seam
gloss: Feel the exact line at which one place stops being itself. A student who has it stops walking into doorways she did not know were there.

effects.gloss: Feel the exact line at which one place stops being itself, and start noticing exactly how well warded the ones you do see actually are.

name: Count the Absences
gloss: Enumerate the doorways that used to be there. A threshold that has been closed leaves a shape in the wall even after the door is gone.

effects.gloss: Enumerate the doorways that used to be there. A threshold that has been closed leaves a shape in the wall even after the door itself is gone.

name: Count the Doors
gloss: Enumerate every threshold in a place at once — its gates, its grave-lines, the seams nobody built on purpose.

effects.gloss: Enumerate every threshold in a place at once, and know which of them would actually hold a lock.

name: Read the Binding
gloss: Read a closed threshold for what it was closed against, and by whom, and how long ago they stopped renewing it.

effects.gloss: Read a closed threshold for what it was closed against, and by whom, and how long ago they stopped renewing it — the strength of the warding is right there in the reading.

name: Read the Unmarked Door
gloss: Find the door that is not there anymore by the way the wall still remembers its shape.

effects.gloss: Find the door that isn't there anymore by the way the wall still remembers its shape. Nothing needs to open for a whole place's worth of closed thresholds to become legible at once.

name: Erase Two Doors
gloss: Find exactly where two thresholds' worth of memory could be erased from the wall — precisely enough that erasing them becomes simple bookkeeping for whoever is equipped to do it.

effects.gloss: Locate two thresholds' worth of memory in the wall precisely enough that erasing them becomes simple bookkeeping for whoever a sapper hands the working to.
A mage who already holds enough of this cell's craft can tell, from a hole in the wall alone, whether a gate could have been opened there at all.

name: Stand in the Doorway
gloss: Hold the seam itself, neither inside nor out — a stance from which exactly how strong the warding on either side is finally becomes legible.

effects.gloss: Hold the seam itself, neither inside nor out. From that standing alone, exactly how strong the warding on either side is finally becomes legible.
Once the warding is legible from where you are standing, so is how far a single step through it would carry.

name: Hold the Threshold
gloss: Hold the seam itself long enough that its ward becomes as legible as everything standing on either side of it.

effects.gloss: Hold the seam itself long enough that its ward becomes as legible as everything on either side of it — and from there, exactly how far a step through would carry.

name: Erase the Standing Gate
gloss: Locate exactly where a standing gate could be erased, and mark exactly how far a step through it would once have carried, in the same working.

effects.gloss: Locate exactly where a standing gate could be erased, and measure exactly how far a step through it would once have carried. Nothing else in the grid maps a threshold's removal this precisely before it happens.
What the ward used to protect becomes visible again, once — the last thing a sealed gate reveals before whatever comes next removes even the memory of standing there.

name: Weigh the Attention
gloss: Tell whether you are being listened to, and by how much of a mind.

effects.gloss: The first filter: whether a mind is listening, and how much of it. Nothing is taught yet, but the lesson's true speed is already legible.

name: Follow the Thought
gloss: Watch a thought move through a mind that is not yours. The best professors have always seemed to know exactly where a student got lost; this is how.

effects.gloss: Watch a thought travel a mind that is not yours. A professor who can trace the path can also see exactly where a taught lesson would hold.

name: Note the Silence
gloss: Notice what a mind has gone quiet about. What a scholar refuses to think about is exactly where a hole is easiest to cut.

effects.gloss: Notice what a mind has gone quiet about. What a scholar refuses to think about is where the hole will be cut, and now that place is marked.

name: Mark the Avoidance
gloss: Learn a mind well enough to know exactly which subject it steers around. The avoidance is a map of what it is protecting.

effects.gloss: Learn a mind well enough to know exactly which subject it steers around. What is being protected is now marked for whoever is unmaking it.

name: Read the Surface
gloss: Watch what is already at the front of a mind, without taking any of it. Nothing is broken and nothing is missed — which is what makes the watching itself so hard to prosecute.

effects.gloss: Watch what is already at the front of a mind, without taking any of it. Nothing is broken, nothing missed — and the watching makes a deeper reach visible to anything built for one.

name: Hush the Witness
gloss: Learn a mind's avoidances well enough that forcing an answer out of it stops requiring its cooperation. The second theft vector, and the one that leaves nothing intact.

effects.gloss: Once a mind's refusals are catalogued in full, forcing an answer out of it stops requiring its cooperation.
A scholar who already knows enough of her own mentem practice can drill a sealed mind's blind spots on command — but only with that much of the craft in hand.

name: Open the Locked Room
gloss: Go past what a scholar is thinking to what she has decided not to think about. The first of the two theft vectors, and the one that leaves the victim intact.

effects.gloss: Go past what a scholar is thinking to what she has decided not to think about, and the gap itself turns out to be exactly measurable in lesson-speed.
The deeper theft only opens once the surface reading is already active in the same mind — a filter behind the first filter.

name: Count the Silences
gloss: Tally every silence in a lecture hall at once — who is listening, who has stopped, and who never started.

effects.gloss: A tally of every silence in a lecture hall — legible only once you already know which minds in it are actually listening. From there, the hall's true teaching speed is obvious.

name: The Last Secret
gloss: Find the one thing a mind has organized its entire defense around keeping back, and mark it in the same working that finds it.

effects.gloss: The last secret a mind can keep, found and marked in the same instant. Nothing else in the grid opens a hole this precisely.
Once a mind is known this precisely, exactly how much could still be taught from it becomes obvious too — for whatever good that does the mind that has been opened.

name: Hear the Name Spoken
gloss: Notice that a thing has a name at all, which most people go their whole lives without doing.

effects.gloss: Notice that a thing has a name at all, which most people go their whole lives without doing — and once noticed, writing it down accurately stops being guesswork.

name: Spell the Lesser Name
gloss: Set down a use-name accurately enough that a scribe who never met the thing can copy it without spoiling it.

effects.gloss: Set down a use-name accurately enough that a scribe who never met the thing can copy it without spoiling it — accurate enough, too, that a listener can be told to hold it exactly this way.

name: Unhear the Name
gloss: Notice a name by the shape of its absence — the gap left in a conversation that is carefully never naming something.

effects.gloss: Notice a name by the shape of its absence — the gap left in a conversation that is carefully never naming something.

name: Derive the True Name
gloss: Work a true name out from first principles rather than being told it. Slow, and the only method that does not put you in someone's debt.

effects.gloss: Work a true name out from first principles rather than being told it. Slow, and the only method that puts nobody in your debt — and the method itself becomes teachable once derived.

name: Forget the Lesser Name
gloss: Learn a name well enough to know exactly which syllable, mispronounced, makes it stop working.

effects.gloss: Learn a name well enough to know exactly which syllable, mispronounced, makes it stop working. The gap between the true name and the near-miss is where a stolen copy hides.

name: The Catalogue of Names
gloss: Order names against one another so that a new one can be found by where the gap in the shelf is. Libraries built on it outlive the mages who filled them.

effects.gloss: Order names against one another so a new one can be found by where the gap in the shelf is. Every copyist in a library built on it can be told exactly how fast to work.
Once the shelf itself is ordered, whoever controls it can also tell precisely which name has quietly gone missing from it.

name: Erase the Ledger
gloss: Find exactly where an entry could be struck from the ledger cleanly enough that its absence would never read as a gap.

effects.gloss: Mark exactly where an entry could be struck from the ledger without its absence ever reading as a gap — the striking itself is a different working.
A forger who already knows this cell's whole catalogue can rewrite an entry fast enough that nobody checks the date.

name: Read the Whole Shelf
gloss: Read not one name but the whole shelf at once, in the order it was built.

effects.gloss: Read not one name but the whole shelf at once — audible only once the catalogue's own rhythm is already legible to you.

name: Unwrite the Name
gloss: Mark a name for both copying and erasure in the same working — though the taking and the removing each still belong to workings of their own.

effects.gloss: Mark a name for both copying and erasure in the same working. Nothing else in the grid locates a removal this precisely while marking the copy in the same breath.
Once a name is unwritten, exactly how well anything built to conceal it will work finally becomes legible — the concealment itself is an older, separate working.

name: Taste the Soil
gloss: Know what the ground under a field will give up before a season is wasted on it.

effects.gloss: Know what the ground under a field will give up before a season is wasted on it — the yield becomes legible before the digging starts.

name: Mark the Hollow
gloss: Notice which page of the hillside is already hollow, or wants to be. Where a foundation cannot be set is where a floor most easily gives way.

effects.gloss: Notice which page of the hillside is already hollow, or wants to be. Where a foundation cannot be set is where a floor most easily gives way.

name: Survey the Strata
gloss: Read a hillside as the stack of pages it is, and say which page the good stone is on.

effects.gloss: Read a hillside as the stack of pages it is. Once you can say which page holds the good stone, you can also say how fast a foundation could be set on it.

name: Find the Deep Seam
gloss: Follow a vein down past where digging by guess stops paying. Whole universities have been sited on one casting of this.

effects.gloss: Follow a vein down past where digging by guess stops paying. Whole universities have been sited on one casting of this, and the yield of the whole seam is visible at once.

name: Read the Fault
gloss: See where the ground intends to fail. Knowing where a wall cannot stand is the cheapest possible way to learn where it can — and it sits at tier 3 deliberately, so that orcs, whose depth ceiling is 3, can reach a build-rate working at all.

effects.gloss: See where the ground intends to fail. Knowing where a wall cannot stand is the cheapest possible way to learn where it can, and the whole cell reads clearer for anyone standing near it.

name: Set the Yield Tables
gloss: Cross-index every seam ever found against what it actually paid out, so the yield of a new one is a lookup rather than a guess.

effects.gloss: Tables cross-indexing every seam ever found against what it actually paid out. From here, the yield of any vein anywhere in the world is a lookup, not a guess.
Once the fault lines of a place are already mapped, the same tables say how fast a wall could stand there.

name: Strip the Hollow
gloss: Read a hollow down to what is structurally still there, so a sapper's crew knows exactly what is left to finish.

effects.gloss: Read a hollow down to what is structurally still there. What is left standing after that is exactly what a sapper's crew can be told to finish.
A surveyor who already knows enough of this ground can price the salvage from a hollowing before the digging even starts.

name: Price the Vein
gloss: Set a price on a vein before the first pick strikes it. Worth nothing to a surveyor who has found nothing yet.

effects.gloss: Set a price on a vein before the first pick strikes it — audible only once the seam's yield is already known to someone in the room.

name: Collapse the Map
gloss: The full map of where ground will give way, cross-referenced against how fast the surface above it could still be built.

effects.gloss: The full map of where this ground will give way, cross-referenced against exactly how fast the surface above it could still be built. Nothing else in the grid predicts a collapse this precisely.
What collapses also releases whatever the hollow was hiding — a last yield, once, from ground that will not give again.

name: The Second Shadow
gloss: Notice that something in the room is casting one shadow more than it is entitled to. Half the students who learn it stop sleeping well; the other half stop being surprised by anything.

name: What the Shadow Remembers
gloss: A shadow is a record of an absence, and records can be interrogated. Ask an empty patch of floor what stood in it, and it will tell you the shape, though never the name.

name: Look Along the Shadow
gloss: Sight down a shadow toward the thing that is casting it, and keep going. What is on the far side of the wall is not hidden from the shadow, only from you, and the shadow can be asked.

name: The Unlit Line
gloss: Perceive, continuously and without effort, which line through a room no eye is currently on — and be on it. Nothing about the mage is hidden. She is simply never where the looking is happening.

name: The Shadow Before the Thing
gloss: Some shadows arrive first. A raid throws one across a floor three days ahead of itself, and a mage who has learned to read the early ones is standing somewhere else by the time the caster gets there. This is where shadow stops being optics and starts being fate.

name: Feel the Air Go Tight
gloss: The small pull in a room in the moment before something is cast in it. Students describe it as a held breath that is not theirs, and the ones who never feel it are usually the ones who die indoors.

name: Price the Working
gloss: Say what a spell cost the mage who cast it. Half of scholarship is knowing which rival results were expensive, because those are the ones nobody bothered to fake.

name: The Residue in the Room
gloss: Perceive what was cast in a place after the casting is over — a day after, in a still room, three weeks. Most of what a university knows about its neighbours was picked up off a floor.

name: Know the Hand That Cast It
gloss: Every mage casts with an accent. This reads it, and names the school, the teacher, and often the individual. Raids are attributed by it, and at least two wars in the archive were begun on a careful misreading of one.

name: Turn the Coat
gloss: Move a beast's coat into a season it is not in. The wool comes off thick in high summer and the animal spends the rest of the year disagreeing with the weather.

name: The Willing Ox
gloss: Change what a beast is shaped to pull. The change is worn, not granted: the shoulders go back to being an ox's shoulders in a season, and the carter is expected to know when.

name: The Changed Kennel
gloss: Turn a kennel into something no one will call a kennel by morning. The dogs are still the dogs, which is the part that unsettles the people who have to feed them afterwards.

name: What the Beast Remembers
gloss: Hold a herd in its changed shape long enough to march it somewhere. Every animal so held is counting down to its own shape, and a field commander's whole skill is in knowing the count.

name: Sweeten the Cistern
gloss: Turn foul water into water. Not clean water — water, which is a lower standard than the phrase suggests and has founded more towns than any other working in the cell.

name: Thicken the Ford
gloss: Change a river into something that will bear a loaded cart. It bears the cart and not the carter, or the carter and not the cart, depending on which the caster was thinking about.

name: The Standing River
gloss: Turn a current into a thing that has stopped agreeing to be crossed. It is not a wall and it is not frozen; it is a river with its mind changed, and it changes back.

name: The River Remembers Salt
gloss: Any water that was ever sea can be persuaded that it still is. Persuading it is cheap; persuading it back is a matter for the next generation of whoever farms the valley.

name: Turn the Wind
gloss: Change which way the air has decided to go. Mills, sails, and drying-floors all run on the assumption that this is legal here, and half of them stop when it is not.

name: The Mild Season
gloss: Turn a bad year into an ordinary one. The weather it was going to be is not destroyed, only converted, and the standing question in the literature is where the conversion is paid for.

name: The Air That Carries Nothing
gloss: Change air into air that will not pass a sound or a scent along. Everything inside it is still there and still shouting; the air has simply stopped consenting to relay it.

name: The Storm Turned Inward
gloss: Change a storm's argument with the horizon into an argument with the ground beneath it. Weather so turned keeps its old heading and comes back around on the caster within the week.

name: Borrowed Hands
gloss: Take the hands of a trade you never trained in. Copyists hired for their fingers rather than their letters are a known and faintly disreputable feature of large libraries.

name: The Body for the Work
gloss: Change a body to suit its labour rather than changing the labour to suit the body. Masons who hold it finish walls early and are unfit for anything else by fifty.

name: Wear Another Face
gloss: Change the flesh, not the appearance of it. An illusionist's version washes off in a hard rain; this one has to be worn back, and the walk is what gives you away either way.

name: The Long Body
gloss: Rearrange a body so that it wears at a different rate. It is not the same thing as being young, and every scholar who has held it says so in exactly the same tired sentence.

name: The Shape That Holds
gloss: A change that no longer has to be renewed, only endured. Transformation is never finished, so what this actually buys is a body that has stopped trying to finish going back.

name: Turn the Small Luck
gloss: Change a trivial fate into a different trivial fate. The dropped cup lands whole and the milk is sour instead. Nothing is gained; something is exchanged, which is the entire cell in one sentence and the reason it is taught first.

name: Change the Debt
gloss: Move a fate off the person it was addressed to and onto a thing that person owns. The ruin still happens. It happens to the barn.

name: The Later Appointment
gloss: Change the hour at which a fate falls due, and nothing else about it whatsoever. The appointment is kept; it has merely been rescheduled, and the literature is unanimous that it will not be rescheduled twice.

name: Divide It Among the Heirs
gloss: Change a fate that belongs to a person into one that belongs to a line, so that it is paid in instalments by people who did not incur it. Houses that hold this working are large, prosperous, and quiet about why.

name: The Fate That Was Yours
gloss: Exchange one whole fate for another whole fate, entire, with something that has one. Both parties survive the working and neither is afterwards the person the archive holds on file. The archive is not wrong.

name: Season the Green Wood
gloss: Turn green timber into seasoned timber without spending the years on it. The beam is honest about having been hurried, and a good carpenter can hear it in the tap of a mallet.

name: The Second Harvest
gloss: Change a crop into a crop the year actually needs, after the year has made itself clear. Nothing is created; a field of straw becomes a smaller field of grain.

name: The Grown Beam
gloss: Change a living tree into the shape a joint wants, and leave it living while it takes. Halls built this way cannot be repaired by anyone who does not also hold the working.

name: The Thicket That Was a Road
gloss: Turn a road into the wood it was cut from. It remembers being a road and is one again inside three seasons, which is the whole trouble with using it in a siege you intend to win slowly.

name: Bank the Forge
gloss: Turn a fire's heat into a slower and longer heat of the same total. Smelting that would take a week takes a week, and takes one charge of fuel to do it.

name: The Cold Flame
gloss: Turn a fire's heat into its opposite while it goes on burning. It still consumes; it has only been changed about what. Standing in it is survivable and is not pleasant.

name: Teach the Fire What to Eat
gloss: Change what a fire counts as fuel. Stone will do, once it has been told; the fire is slower about stone and does not otherwise object.

name: The Heat That Was a Hearth
gloss: Every fire in a building was lit by somebody for a reason. This changes the reason, and leaves the fire exactly where its owner put it.

name: Turn the Diagram
gloss: Change a mechanism's appearance into the appearance of its own structure. Students stop asking what is inside it, because what is inside it is now what they are looking at.

name: The Lecture Made Visible
gloss: Turn an argument into something the room can watch happening. It is the same argument and it is not improved; it has only stopped needing to be held in the head to be followed.

name: Wear the Room
gloss: Change your image into the image of whatever is behind you. It fails on anyone who has been looking at you continuously, which is a shorter list than it sounds.

name: The Image That Argues Back
gloss: Turn a demonstration into one that changes in response to the student's error. The lecturer is still doing the work; she has merely stopped being in the room while it is done.

name: Change What the Wall Means
gloss: A wall raised against weather can be persuaded it was raised against people. It was not, and it knows, so the persuasion has to be renewed about as often as a sentry is changed.

name: The Door That Was a Window
gloss: Change a threshold's kind rather than its state. Declares no portal effect and never will: opening onto another sky is Rego Limen, and contracts.md §8 keeps it there on purpose.

name: Which Side the Courtyard Is On
gloss: Change which side of a boundary a place is on without moving the boundary or the place. Two sieges in the record were settled by an argument about a courtyard, conducted entirely in this working.

name: The Seam Made a Hinge
gloss: Change a boundary into a joint, so that it bends where it used to hold. It bends back, and the fortress it was worked on is afterwards a fortress with a habit.

name: Turn the Difficulty
gloss: Change a problem's shape in a mind until it is a problem that mind already knows how to have. Nothing has been solved. The solving now costs what an easy problem costs.

name: The Changed Appetite
gloss: Change what a mind wants to think about, rather than what it is permitted to. Compulsion is Rego and shows; this does not show, including to the scholar it was worked on.

name: Translate the Expert
gloss: Change another scholar's knowledge into the shape your own mind keeps things in. She keeps hers. What you carry off is a translation, and translations lose things. Universities that count two theft vectors are counting the two that are prosecutable.

name: The Mind Made a Library
gloss: Change a mind's arrangement into a catalogue's. It is reversible in the way everything in Muto is reversible, and the scholars who reverse it go on thinking in shelves regardless.

name: Alter One Letter
gloss: Change a true name by the smallest amount that is still a change. The thing changes by the same amount. Most of what is known about naming was learned by doing this to unimportant objects and writing down how they were afterwards slightly different unimportant objects.

name: Lend the Name
gloss: Give a thing your name to hold for an afternoon. Nothing that hunts by naming can tell you from a chair, and nothing that hunts by naming can tell the chair from you, which is the half that has to be planned for.

name: Call It Iron Until It Is
gloss: Change the true name of poor rock to the true name of iron and then wait. It becomes iron at roughly the rate the claim goes unchallenged, and stops the moment anyone successfully contradicts it. Assayers are paid well and are not popular.

name: Trade True Names
gloss: Exchange true names with another mage, so that each becomes the other in every way naming can reach. Compulsion follows the name. Skill does not. Both parties spend the arrangement being ordered about in a discipline they cannot practise.

name: The Second True Name
gloss: Hold a second true name without surrendering the first. Nothing in the discipline says a thing may have two. Nothing in the discipline says it may not. The holder is betting a great deal on which of those two silences is the load-bearing one.

name: Soften the Stone
gloss: Turn cut stone briefly workable. The masons have the length of an afternoon and no more, and every quarry in the subset has a bell for it.

name: Turn the Poor Ore
gloss: Change worthless rock into ore that is merely bad. Never into good ore: the working improves a thing by one step and has never once been made to take two.

name: The Stone That Was Sand
gloss: Turn a riverbank into ashlar. It knows it was sand and intends to be sand again, so a wall raised from it is a wall you have agreed to build twice.

name: Turn the Ground Under Them
gloss: Change standing ground into the sand it was before anyone stood on it. The besiegers of Halvard's Rock reported that the ground did not open; it simply stopped having been a floor.

name: Turn the Shadow
gloss: Change the direction a shadow falls without moving what casts it. Nobody notices, in the sense that nobody can afterwards say what it was they noticed.

name: The Shadow of Something Else
gloss: Change what your shadow is a shadow of. The old shape is still in it and comes back at the hour the working was first laid, which is why this is taught alongside a clock.

name: Give the Shade Weight
gloss: Turn shade into something with an opinion about being walked through. It is cold in the way deep water is cold, and it is exactly as deep as whatever cast it is tall.

name: Trade Shadows
gloss: Exchange your shadow for another's and step where theirs may go. The other party keeps yours for the duration, and anything that hunts by shadow can still find you with it.

name: Turn the Working
gloss: Change a small spell into a different small spell while it is still being cast. The first thing every apprentice does with it is ruin a working she had already finished paying for.

name: Convert the Form
gloss: Change what a working is about without changing what it does — Ignem to Aquam and back again. The grid is not a filing system for scholars; this is the working that proves it.

name: Turn the Incoming
gloss: Change a hostile working, in flight, into a harmless one of the same size. It arrives on time and does something else, and the caster is not told which.

name: The Second Tradition
gloss: Change how a working is performed rather than what it performs: a memorised formula rewritten as a room in a palace. The translation costs about a third of the working, in both directions, every time.

name: The Common Root
gloss: Change any working into any other by way of what the two were before they were told apart. Every scholar who has published on it has published the same warning, in the same words: the way back is not the way you came.

name: Founder the Horse
gloss: Unmake the wind in a beast at a gallop. The rider is not thrown and is not hurt; she is simply on foot, in a field, a long way from her line.

name: Nothing Takes the Scent
gloss: Unmake what you left in the air behind you. The hounds are not confused — a confused hound casts about. These sit down.

name: Empty the Pasture
gloss: Wither a holding's beasts across a stretch of ground, over an afternoon, without a mark on any of them. A siege begun in spring is decided by this in autumn.

name: Nothing Answers the Horn
gloss: Unmake what was called. Warhorses, hounds, the summoned things a Nomen mage keeps on a name — all of it goes, and the field is very quiet, and the horn is blown twice more before anyone stops.

name: Thirst
gloss: Unmake the water a body is carrying, beginning with the water it can spare. There is a good deal of it, and then there is not.

name: Unwrite
gloss: Take the water out of ink. The page is not burned, the binding is not cut, and the book is a stack of blank leaves taking up exactly as much shelf as it did. Raiders who cannot carry a library and will not burn one use this.

name: The Dry Season
gloss: Unmake the water in the ground itself, across a stretch of it. The wells go first, then the shallow roots, then the arguments about whose fault it is.

name: Leave Them the Salt
gloss: Unmake every fresh water in reach and leave behind only what cannot be drunk. A holding treated this way is not stormed. It is walked into, eleven days later.

name: Take the Breath
gloss: Unmake the air a body has already drawn. She does not gasp — there is nothing left to gasp with — and it is the surprise on the face that wardens remember afterwards.

name: Unmake the Gale
gloss: Take the weather out of weather that was aimed at you. The storm does not break and does not turn; it stops being a storm, midway, above the men it was meant for.

name: The Airless Room
gloss: Unmake the air inside a closed space and hold it unmade. It is the cheapest working on this ladder and the one universities most often decline to teach, for reasons that are about doors rather than about air.

name: The Sky Withdraws
gloss: Unmake the air over a field. Nothing flies, nothing carries, nothing burns, and no order shouted at the far end of the line is heard at this one. Both sides suffer it equally, which is the whole of the argument against it.

name: Wither the Hand
gloss: Take the strength out of the hand that is holding the sword. It is not a wound, and it does not mend the way a wound does.

name: The Long Fever
gloss: Unmake a body slowly enough that the physicians name the illness, argue about it, and are wrong in a way that takes them six weeks to be wrong in.

name: Take the Years
gloss: Unmake the decades a body still had in front of it. She is not injured. She is older than she was this morning, and the work she was going to do is not going to be done by her.

name: The Hand That Wrote It
gloss: The standard answer to a scholar who is the last surviving instance of something. It is not a duel and it is not a battle. It is a piece of archival policy, carried out by someone who was paid for it and told very little.

name: Spoil the Omen
gloss: Unmake a sign before anyone has read it. The augur is not wrong. There is simply nothing there for her to be right about.

name: Take the Luck
gloss: Unmake a person's share of things going well. Nothing happens to her. Things merely stop not happening to her.

name: Nothing Is Owed
gloss: Every fate is a debt something means to collect. Unmake the debt and the collector goes elsewhere; unmake enough of them and the world stops keeping accounts in your name at all.

name: Where Nothing Turns Out
gloss: Unmake, across a field, the tendency of events to come to anything. Charges arrive late. Signals are not seen. Both sides bleed and neither wins, and the mage who cast it was not trying to win either.

name: The Unmade Discovery
gloss: It does not destroy a node. It unmakes the arrival of one. Somewhere a scholar who was going to derive something puts her pen down for a reason she could give you, and it is not the reason. The universities that do not hold this working cannot prove that they do not.

name: Wither the Row
gloss: Unmake a row of a crop at the root. Done at the edge of a field it reads as bad drainage, and that is the point of doing it at the edge.

name: Take the Haft
gloss: Unmake the wood in a thing that everyone thinks of as iron. Spears become spearheads, ladders become rungs, and a siege engine becomes a great deal of rope and a heap of fittings.

name: The Failed Harvest
gloss: Wither a season across a stretch of ground. The dead are counted the following winter, attributed to the weather, and no mage is named anywhere in the accounting.

name: The Shelves Give Way
gloss: A library is stone and glass and a very great deal of wood. Unmake the presses, the shelving, and the boards the bindings are stretched over, and what is on the floor afterwards is not a collection. It is loose paper in the dark, in an order nobody wrote down.

name: Snuff
gloss: Take the fire out of a flame. The wick is not wet and no smoke rises, and the room is a room that a moment ago had a light in it.

name: Take the Warmth
gloss: Unmake the heat inside a body rather than the body. Corpus withers the flesh; this leaves the flesh entirely alone and takes away the thing that was keeping it going.

name: The Unburnt Library
gloss: Unmake a fire that is already in the stacks. Perdo is how a library is saved rather less often than it is how one is lost, and it is the same working either way — the same training, the same hour of practice, different people holding it.

name: Nothing Will Catch
gloss: Take the willingness to burn out of a place. Nothing here will catch: not the thatch, not the oil, not the shelves. Not the hearth either, and not the lamp a scholar reads by. Universities that keep this standing have not had a fire in a century and cannot say what the century cost them.

name: Take the Likeness
gloss: Unmake the resemblance between a thing and its picture. The portrait is still a portrait. It is simply not of anyone.

name: The Quiet Working
gloss: Unmake the sound and the light a casting makes, and not the casting. Wardens who watch are expensive and wardens who listen are cheap, and this is the working that decided which kind a university hires.

name: Unmake the Demonstration
gloss: The professor's hands still move and the working still happens; there is nothing to see it by. Aimed at demonstrations, and afterwards at the engraved plates in the treatises made from them. The working survives. The picture of it does not, and after one generation those are the same thing.

name: No One Can Describe It
gloss: Unmake the image of a place and leave the place. Scouts come back having seen nothing they can put in a report; two maps of it disagree with each other and with the ground. The hall is exactly where it always was, and the company sent to hold it does not arrive.

name: Fray the Edge
gloss: Wear at a boundary until it stops being certain about where it is. Contains no portal-stability effect, and may never gain one (contracts.md §1.6).

effects.gloss: A boundary loses a little of its certainty about where it runs, and whatever leaned on that certainty loses a little too.

name: Forget the Frame
gloss: Quietly unmake a room's memory of where its own boundary runs, rather than wrenching the boundary open. A boundary that has been fought remembers being fought; this one is never fought at all.

effects.gloss: The caster passes a threshold that never registers her passing, because the threshold has quietly forgotten it has an inside and an outside.

name: Unhinge
gloss: Take the held-shut out of a shut thing. Wards fail first at the place they were joined.

effects.gloss: A ward's joinery loses whatever kept it holding itself shut, and fails exactly there first.

name: Crack the Seam
gloss: Find the place where a threshold was joined to the ground on either side of it, and unmake that joint. The ground on both sides remembers being cracked long after the threshold is repaired.

effects.gloss: The seam between a threshold and the earth it stands in stops holding, and the ground either side of it goes with it.

name: The Open Wound
gloss: Leave a threshold unmade rather than merely opened, so that the ground on both sides of it stays wrong for a while.

effects.gloss: The threshold is not opened so much as left unfinished, and the wrongness of that spreads a little into the ground either side.

name: Nothing Holds
gloss: Unmake every seam in reach at once. Defenders describe it as the moment a fortress stops being one building and starts being a pile of walls.

effects.gloss: Every seam a fortress was joined at lets go within the same breath.
Whatever was standing at the keystone of the structure is struck along with the seams.
A mage this deep in Perdo Limen finds the collapse spreads further than she aimed it, once she has enough of the discipline to stop needing to aim it at all.

name: The Severed Hold
gloss: Unmake the grip a threshold has on the structure around it, rather than the threshold itself. Worth nothing until the grip has actually been seen — and ruinous once it has.

effects.gloss: Once the threshold's hold on its structure is understood, severing it drops whatever it was bearing all at once.
The ground around the severed hold keeps refusing to bear weight for as long as the understanding of it lasts.

name: The Forgotten Threshold
gloss: The deepest hollow-ground working in Perdo Limen: a threshold's collapse held open indefinitely, so the ground either side of it forgets it was ever a place that could be crossed.

effects.gloss: The ground on both sides of the threshold stays wrong indefinitely, and the wrongness widens the longer it is left.
Whatever tries to cross where the threshold used to be is struck by the absence of a place to stand.
Once the scale of the hollow is understood, no builder in the universe trusts ground this practiced at swallowing thresholds, and construction everywhere slows a little for it.

name: The Shut World
gloss: The standing-gate track's final working: a place unmade so thoroughly that nothing may ever cross where it used to be, portal or otherwise. It contains no portal effect and grants none — it only makes certain, forever, that one could never open here.

effects.gloss: A place stops being a place that can be crossed, arrived at, or opened onto, permanently and everywhere within the working's reach.
Once what is being shut is truly understood, whatever still tries to stand at the threshold is struck by the fact that there is no longer a threshold there to stand at.

name: Blunt the Edge
gloss: Take the sharpness out of an attention. The victim is not hurt and cannot say what is wrong, only that thinking has begun to cost more than it did.

effects.gloss: The first cut Perdo Mentem teaches: a mind loses just enough acuity to notice the loss and not name it.

name: Nothing to Find
gloss: Seal a mind against the record it would otherwise leave, so that there is nothing later to erase. Where the misplaced hour edits a memory afterward, this refuses to let one form.

effects.gloss: The caster's own passage through a room stops registering as a memory in anyone who witnessed it.

name: The Misplaced Hour
gloss: Unmake a stretch of a mind's own record of itself. Small, deniable, and the first thing every inquiry into a scholar's death asks about.

effects.gloss: An hour goes missing from a memory. The hole is small enough that most minds paper over it themselves.

name: Scatter the Lesson
gloss: Undo a thing at the moment it is being taught, in every mind in the room. Aimed at lecture halls, and used on them.

effects.gloss: Every mind in the hall loses the same sentence at the same moment, and no two of them lose it the same way.

name: The Unheard Word
gloss: A general erosion of a room's willingness to be taught in, that only shows once a mage has learned to see it: a university fluent in unmaking lessons finds its own lessons will not stick either.

effects.gloss: The caster's own teaching thins, in the same coin she spends elsewhere: a hole where a lesson used to land cleanly.

name: Forget the Forgetting
gloss: A meta-erasure: the memory of having unmade a memory, unmade in turn. Worth nothing to a mage working alone, and a great deal to one whose university has learned to notice what she is doing.

effects.gloss: Once the working itself has been perceived, the erasure lands twice as clean, its own trace gone with the rest.
A mind this practiced at unmaking finds new derivations slower; the same hole that empties a victim's head thins its owner's.

name: Unmake the Mind
gloss: Not kill. Unmake — the body walks out of the hall and the scholar does not. This is the working the vision's flagship interdiction forbids by name: Mentem is open to my scholars, but none shall unmake a mind.

effects.gloss: A sine in the victim's head has a hole taken out of it, and the hole does not close.

name: The Empty Room
gloss: The unmaking held open, so that nothing put back into the space stays there either. Universities that permit it do not admit to it.

effects.gloss: The victim's mind is not merely opened; it is kept open, and nothing poured back in survives the night.
The room itself refuses to hold a thought for as long as the working stands.

name: The Unwritten Word
gloss: The deepest working in Perdo Mentem, and the only one that also unmakes its own record of being cast. Reachable only by a mind that has never opened itself to another and never once quarried the world — everyone else finds only the shape of a working with no working inside it.

effects.gloss: There is no impact transient, no struck note — only a sine that was there, and then a silence exactly the shape it left.
The working refuses even its own caster an account of itself; nothing about how it was done can afterward be derived from having done it.

name: Mispronounce
gloss: Damage a name slightly, in the mouth of whoever is trying to use it on you.

effects.gloss: A name loses a little of its grip on the tongue trying to use it, and the caster is a little harder to call.

name: Shed the Use-Name
gloss: Unmake the name you are called by. Colleagues still recognise the face; nothing that works by naming can find you at all.

effects.gloss: The use-name is unmade outright; anything that would have found the caster by it finds nothing where the name used to be.

name: Take Back the Word
gloss: Unmake a single claim spoken about you, rather than the name it was spoken of. A retraction with teeth: aimed at one rumor at a time, not at the name that carries all of them.

effects.gloss: One spoken claim is struck out of whoever repeats it, mid-sentence, without touching anything else they know.

name: Close the Throat
gloss: Seal a name so thoroughly that no mouth can shape it at all, rather than merely hiding the person it names. The nomen half of a doctrine Perdo Mentem shares: a mind sealed at both ends.

effects.gloss: The name will not form in any mouth that tries it, not even a hostile one that already half-knows the sound.

name: Unsay the Name
gloss: Turn the working on someone else's true name. What is left is not injured; it is less.

effects.gloss: The true name is struck directly, and what answers to it afterward answers to less of itself.
Once a true name has actually been parsed, unsaying it also quietly conceals the caster who did the unsaying.

name: Nothing to Call You
gloss: Both halves of the sealed-mind doctrine at once, and worth nothing until each has been understood on its own: a mind closed at the throat and closed to reading, held together.

effects.gloss: Once a mind's sealing is properly understood, the seal itself becomes near-total: nothing that could name the caster still can.
A mind sealed this completely against being read from outside finds it harder to read anything new from outside either.

name: The Nameless
gloss: Hold your own unnaming indefinitely. Cheap to maintain, ruinous to explain to an heir, and the reason some archmages have no biography.

effects.gloss: The unnaming holds open on its own, at almost no ongoing cost, for as long as the mage cares to keep it.

name: The Silence With No Owner
gloss: The deepest sealed-mind working in Perdo Nomen: a silence so complete it no longer has a caster to attribute it to. Nothing that could ask whose working this is finds an answer, including the one who cast it.

effects.gloss: The caster becomes, functionally, un-attributable: nothing that could trace this working back to her can.
A mage this deep into the sealed-mind track finds the silence bites back on its own, striking anything that tries to force the name loose.

name: No One Answers
gloss: The nameless-road track's final working: unmake not one name but the practice of naming that place or person at all. The deepest working in Perdo Nomen along this route, and the reason some questions simply stop being askable.

effects.gloss: There is no longer a name for anything that would need answering to; the question of who this is stops being a question with an answer.
Once the scale of the unnaming is understood, nobody can be taught to call the caster by anything at all, and teaching that depends on the name fails outright.

name: Crumble
gloss: Take the bind out of mortar, one course at a time.

effects.gloss: A wall loses whatever was holding its courses together, and does not fall so much as stop insisting on standing.

name: Open the Ground
gloss: Unmake the ground's willingness to be stood on, across a stretch of it, for as long as attention holds.

effects.gloss: A stretch of ground stops being reliably solid; nobody falls through it so much as it stops promising not to.

name: Strip the Vein
gloss: Take the value out of a seam of stone rather than the stone itself — what is left still stands and is worth nothing to build with. The mason's discipline, worked backward.

effects.gloss: A permanent thinness enters the universe's supply of good stone: it is still there, and none of it is good anymore.

name: Pull Down the Arch
gloss: Unmake the one stone the rest were argued into leaning on. Cheaper than unmaking a building, and identical in outcome.

effects.gloss: One stone stops holding its argument, and the building it was supporting discovers it never had one.

name: Take More Than Is Set
gloss: Quarry past the line a mason would stop at. Cheap as a single theft, but a civilization fluent enough in Perdo Terram to know what it's doing finds its own construction pays for the habit too.

effects.gloss: Once a civilization has enough Perdo Terram in its hands to know what it is doing, its own construction slows: the habit of taking too much does not stay confined to enemy walls.

name: Break the Load
gloss: Flaw a shipment of quarried stone so it fails only once it has been trusted — built into a wall, leaned on, believed in. Worth nothing until someone has looked closely enough to see the flaw.

effects.gloss: Once the flaw is noticed for what it is, every shipment behind it is quietly suspect, and the universe's stone is worth less across the board.
The wall built on the flawed course fails exactly where the flaw was left, on a day nobody chose.

name: The Swallowed Hall
gloss: Take a building's foundation out from under it and leave the hole behaving badly afterwards. The standard answer to a library that cannot be carried away.

effects.gloss: The ground beneath a hall keeps not-holding for as long as the working stands, well past the moment the hall itself is gone.
Whatever load-bearing thing is struck loses its argument for existing at all.

name: The Long Fall
gloss: Open the ground and keep it open, past the reach of any working that merely denies a stretch of it. The deepest hollow-ground working before a civilization gives up building at all.

effects.gloss: The ground does not merely refuse to hold weight; it keeps refusing, indefinitely, in a widening circle.
Once the hollow is understood for what it is, whatever falls into it falls further than the drop should allow.

name: The Unquarried
gloss: The renunciation the quarried-world track ends in: a civilization that has learned to unmake what quarrying makes possible stops quarrying at all. The deepest working in Perdo Terram, and the strangest — a mastery of stone that ends in refusing it.

effects.gloss: The universe's construction slows permanently and on purpose: nothing further is asked of the ground, ever again.
What is struck is not weakened. It is un-quarried, taken back past the point of ever having been stone that could be set.

name: Thin the Shade
gloss: Wear at what a thing leaves behind it. The shadow is still there and no longer quite belongs to anyone, and the thing that cast it is, by a small amount, less.

name: Lay the Shade
gloss: The dead leave a shape. Unmake the shape. Wardens who do this are paid by the hour and never by the name, and are not asked afterwards what the shape had been doing.

name: Nothing Casts Here
gloss: Unmake every remnant across a stretch of ground and hold it unmade, so that nothing which happens there has an afterward. Fought over twice, such a field is not haunted, and the villages near it find that worse.

name: Make Sure
gloss: A scholar who dies holding something nobody else holds leaves a shade that still, faintly, holds it — enough for a patient Intellego man and a long night in the right graveyard. This unmakes the shade. Whoever commissions it is not being cruel. She is making sure.

name: Let It Lapse
gloss: Do not argue with a working. Unmake the part of it that intends to keep going, and then wait a moment.

name: The Unfinished Sentence
gloss: Unmake a working while it is still being made. Far cheaper than unmaking a finished one, and the reason a duel between equals is decided in the first half-second and watched for the remaining hour.

name: Where Nothing Takes
gloss: Unmake, over a stretch of ground, the willingness of workings to hold at all — your own among them. It declares no portal-stability effect and never will (contracts.md §1.6). The cell stops at three nodes on purpose: further down, unmaking magic stops being a spell and starts being a rule, and rules belong to the god.

name: The Quiet Halter
gloss: Compel a beast to stand where it was put, without rope and without argument. A draft team that does not shy is worth two teams that do, which is why the working appears in building accounts a century before it appears in any bestiary.

name: Drive the Herd
gloss: Move a herd as one thing, over ground no drover would have chosen, without dogs and without losses at the river.

name: The Borrowed Eye
gloss: Send a beast where you would otherwise have to go, and hold it to the errand. A hawk on the ridge is a scout who cannot be bribed, and nobody thinks to look for the scholar who never left her tower.

name: Bring the Pack to Heel
gloss: Call whatever hunts in the country around you and hold it to your order for the length of a fight. Between fights the same binding keeps a university in meat, which is the part the charters actually mention.

name: Turn the Channel
gloss: Send water down the ditch you meant it to take, and keep it there through a season. Irrigation is the oldest application and still the one that pays for the rest.

name: Raise the Weir
gloss: Hold a river at a height it did not agree to. A weir that need not be built of stone can be put where the mill wants it rather than where the ground allows.

name: Stand the Water Off
gloss: Compel water to refuse the shape of a wave, and stand behind it. A wall of held water turns a great deal that a wall of stone does not, and can be dismissed when the siege lifts.

name: The Held Breath
gloss: Compel the water already inside a body to stop moving. Nothing is added and nothing is taken away, which is why three universities record the result as a natural death and the fourth has stopped recording it at all.

name: Shut the Harbour Mouth
gloss: Bind a stretch of water to hold in both directions at once: nothing crosses it, and nothing thrown across it arrives. Coastal universities keep a warden on the working the way inland ones keep a gatekeeper.

name: Set the Wind
gloss: Put the wind where a sail wants it, for as long as the crossing takes. Timber and stone arrive on the day they were promised, which quietly changes what a university is able to plan.

name: Step on the Air
gloss: Compel a column of air to take a footfall. Not flight: one stride that ends somewhere a stride should not reach, and a long argument afterwards about whether you were ever off the ground.

name: Turn the Storm Aside
gloss: Bind weather to go around a place rather than through it. The neighbours get the weather, and the literature on whether that is actionable is longer than the literature on the working.

name: The Held Gale
gloss: Hold a gale in one place and stand inside it. Everything in reach is being pushed at once, the caster included, which is why the working is never taught apart from the stride that gets her out of it.

name: Still the Limb
gloss: Hold a body to its stance, one part at a time — usually your own. Flesh that has been told not to give does not give, and the surgeons found this useful a long time before the duellists did.

name: The Steady Hand
gloss: Compel a hand to keep the line true past the hour at which fatigue would have spoiled it. Every accurate diagram in a great library is downstream of somebody holding this working over somebody else's wrist.

name: Puppet Flesh
gloss: Move a body that is not moving itself. The working does not distinguish between a corpse and a sleeper; the setting calls it necromancy, and the charters distinguish very carefully indeed.

name: The Lengthened Term
gloss: Compel a failing body to keep the arrangement it already has. It adds nothing and heals nothing; it only declines the ending, and the archmages who hold it are careful never to file it beside Puppet Flesh, which is the same insight pointed at a body that has already stopped.

name: The Unclaimed Body
gloss: Bind a body whose owner has gone, and set it to work that nobody is now in a position to object to on its behalf. It is the cheapest labour a university can field, and the only kind that has ever closed one.

name: Hold the Lot
gloss: Hold a chance to the shape it already had. It cannot make an unlikely thing happen; it can stop a likely one from being spoiled, and across a hundred experiments that is worth a great deal more.

name: The Kept Oath
gloss: Bind a promise to its own keeping, so that the breaking of it is the thing that costs. Gods whose worshippers swear on this collect on the oath rather than on the sentiment, and the ledgers show the difference.

name: Turn the Ill Hour Aside
gloss: Take a misfortune that was arriving here and hold it somewhere else for a while. It postpones and does not cancel, and the literature is unusually careful about the difference.

name: The Appointed Hour
gloss: Fix the hour at which a thing ends, and hold it there. Nothing brings it forward and nothing puts it off, and the scholars who take it rarely say afterwards which of those two halves they wanted.

name: The Settled Question
gloss: Bind an outcome and let the world find its own route to it. Every step between here and there still has to be walked; none of them can now go anywhere else, and a god who is owed the ending is owed everything on the way.

name: Set the Graft
gloss: Compel a cutting to take, and to take the way the grafter intended rather than the way the tree would have preferred. An orchard planted under it comes into bearing years early.

name: The Obedient Coppice
gloss: Hold a wood to the lengths a builder asked for, so that the poles come out of it already straight and already the right size. Carpenters describe the result as timber that has been argued with.

name: Close the Hedge
gloss: Bind a hedge to go on closing its own gaps. Nothing that goes through it does so at speed, and nothing that goes through it does so twice.

name: The Standing Timber
gloss: Compel green timber to hold the shape of seasoned timber for as long as it is under load. A hall can then be raised in the season the wood was cut, which is the whole of the trick and also the whole of the risk.

name: Bank the Forge
gloss: Hold a fire at exactly the heat the work wants, for as long as the work takes. Smelters who have it waste no charge and no charcoal, and can say beforehand what a furnace will yield.

name: Hold the Fire Off
gloss: Compel a fire to keep its distance from a named thing. Every library that survives its first arson puts the working on the syllabus permanently, and every library has a first arson.

name: Drive the Flame
gloss: Take a fire somebody else lit and tell it where to go. It costs nothing to start, which makes an enemy's own torches the cheapest armament available on the field.

name: The Walled Fire
gloss: Bind a fire into a standing ring and stand in the middle of it. The same compulsion that keeps it burning where it was put is what keeps it off the mage who put it there.

name: Hold the Likeness
gloss: Compel an image to stay exactly as it was set down, so that the tenth copy of a diagram is still the first. Scriptoria that hold it stop losing figures to the slow drift of careful hands.

name: The Turned Glance
gloss: Compel an eye to travel past you rather than to you. Nothing about you changes; the looking does, and afterwards nobody can say what they were looking at instead.

name: Show the Working
gloss: Hold the image of a working in the air where a class can walk around it. The difference between describing a proof and standing inside one is most of what a professor is for.

name: The Standing Demonstration
gloss: Hold one demonstration steady for a whole term, so that the lecture, the argument about the lecture, and the plates for the book are all taken from the same unmoving thing.

name: Hold the Door
gloss: Compel a threshold to keep meaning what it means, against anything arguing otherwise.

effects.gloss: A floor under a threshold's resolve: it may be pressed, but never below this much give.

name: Step Across
gloss: Treat two thresholds as the same threshold for exactly one stride.

effects.gloss: A floor under how far a single compelled stride reliably carries.

name: Test the Frame
gloss: Refuse to cross until the threshold has been made to argue back, and listen to what it says.

effects.gloss: A cap on how much a tested frame is reinforced in the testing: the point is information, not strength.

name: Open the Hollow
gloss: Argue a threshold not into a doorway but into an absence: the ground on the other side simply is not there.

effects.gloss: A floor under how much ground stays unusable once the hollow is opened.
Opening a hollow costs some of the mage's own defensive resolve; it never rises past this while the hollow stands.

name: Seal the Way
