gloss: Bind a threshold shut and make the binding argue back. The defensive half of the same insight that opens portals, which is why forbidding Limen closes both directions at once.

effects.gloss: A floor under a sealed door's resistance.
Once a sealing is understood well enough to be read, it also steadies the stride that undoes it.
A mage who has held and sealed two thresholds has learned, incidentally, how to be one.

name: Open the Portal
gloss: Hold a threshold open onto a sky that is not yours. Everything the multiverse does to a universe begins here, which is why contracts.md §8 requires this cell in every v1 build.

effects.gloss: A floor under how reliably the gate holds open once argued into existence.

name: The Drowned Threshold
gloss: A hollow ground and a held door are two separate workings until a mage understands the seam between them — and only then does opening one guarantee how much ground stays unusable, at a hard ceiling on her own defenses while it does.

effects.gloss: Once the seam is legible, the hollow ground it opens holds at least this much unusable space.
The same understanding that opens the hollow further caps how well the mage can also defend herself while doing it.

name: The Standing Gate
gloss: A portal that does not have to be argued into existence each time. Declares no portal-stability effect and never will: the raid's termination guarantee is a proof, not an observation (contracts.md §1.6).

effects.gloss: The mage who keeps a gate standing holds herself to a guaranteed minimum readiness, and never further than this — a standing gate is tended, not fortified without limit.
A floor under how fast the gate's own keeper can move to it.

name: The Collapsing Threshold
gloss: The portal cell's deepest working: a gate that opens only onto ground already emptied beneath it. A hard lock, and then you are somewhere else, and the somewhere is a hole.

effects.gloss: A gate on a gate: the crossing is guaranteed to hold this reliably, and guaranteed never to be pushed past this — the hollow ground on the far side is the whole design, not an accident of power.
A floor under how much of the arrival ground stays unusable to whoever is waiting there.

name: Hold the Attention
gloss: Keep a mind on the thing in front of it. Unglamorous, and the single largest effect on how fast a university actually teaches.

effects.gloss: A floor under a lecture: attention wanders, but never below this much of it.

name: Still Your Own Mind
gloss: Discipline a mind to give nothing away, on principle, before there is anything worth taking.

effects.gloss: A floor under a mage's own guardedness: it never slips below this, whatever the provocation.

name: The Patient Lesson
gloss: Compel a mind to keep returning to a difficulty instead of routing around it.

effects.gloss: A deeper floor than mere attention buys: the lesson lands even on a bad day.

name: Kindle Devotion
gloss: Bind an ordinary reverence into a durable one. Gods whose scholars know this working are noticeably better funded, and there is a long literature on whether that is cheating.

effects.gloss: A floor under devotion: the faithful may cool, but never past this line.
Once a room's devotion is legible, it also steadies how fast the room learns.

name: Veil the Thought
gloss: Teach a mind to seal itself the moment it starts to open, so that nothing said aloud carries what was actually thought — at the cost of a hard ceiling on how fast that same mind can afterward be taught.

effects.gloss: A firmer floor than plain stillness: the sealed mind holds its secrecy under real pressure.
A mind trained to seal itself cannot be rushed past this pace, however devoted the teacher.

name: The Locked Ledger
gloss: Turn a sealed mind into a trap rather than a vault: worth nothing until someone tries to read it.

effects.gloss: Once a thief's reach into this mind is legible, at least this much of what they came for turns around on them.
Using a mind as bait costs some of its total secrecy, once the trap has been seen for what it is.

name: The Shared Mind
gloss: Hold teacher and student in one attention, so that the lesson does not have to survive the trip between them.

effects.gloss: The joined attention guarantees the lesson lands, and guarantees it lands no faster than the slower of the two minds.
Two minds that have learned to share attention also share what moves them, once there are enough of them to notice.

name: The Devoted College
gloss: Scale the shared mind past a pair and into a faculty: attention, once compelled at all, compels further.

effects.gloss: A whole college's devotion floors out higher than any two minds could manage alone.
A faculty that shares attention also shares its questions, and never falls below this pace of answering them.

name: The Unspoken Doctrine
gloss: A body of thought held by a whole sealed faculty and never once spoken where it could be copied. The deepest secrecy the grid allows.

effects.gloss: As total a secrecy floor as the grid permits, bought by a ceiling that forbids ever pushing it higher: the doctrine is complete, and complete is all it will ever be.

name: Call by Name
gloss: Say a thing's name in the imperative and have it arrive. The oldest complaint in the literature is that it does not specify in what condition.

effects.gloss: A floor under how much of the summoned thing actually arrives.

name: Keep the Name Close
gloss: Hold your own name in your own keeping, so that it does not answer when someone else uses it. Taught in the same term as Compel by Name, by professors who consider that an ethics curriculum.

effects.gloss: A floor under how well a mage's true name stays her own.

name: Write the Name Down
gloss: Bind a name to a page so firmly that a scribe who cannot pronounce it can still copy it correctly.

effects.gloss: A floor under how fast a bound name can be correctly copied, regardless of the scribe's own skill.

name: Compel by Name
gloss: Hold a mage by her name and take what she knows out through it. The second theft vector, and the one that leaves a mark — which is why a universe may want to close exactly one of the two.

effects.gloss: A floor under how much a compelled name gives up, whatever the victim's own guardedness.
Once the target's name is legible enough to compel, some of the compeller's own secrecy is spent doing it.

name: Hold the Name Whole
gloss: A name held whole against forgetting is the first refusal of decline. It teaches nothing about anyone else — it is a mage learning to keep herself.

effects.gloss: A floor under how fast a faculty can study a subject once it has a name to hold the study by.

A floor of twenty years held against a life's own decline — modest, and the only one of the three life-extension effects that asks nothing of Intellego to trigger, only enough of it already studied to have earned the working.

name: The Bound Servant
gloss: Call a thing by a name it cannot refuse and keep it. In a True Naming universe this is either the strongest working in the subset or the reason your archmage now belongs to someone else.

effects.gloss: A guaranteed minimum take from a fully bound servant, capped so that even total compulsion cannot be pushed past a survivable limit.
A second bound servant arrives more reliably once the first has proven the working holds.

name: The Open Ledger
gloss: A registry of names held in common, worth nothing to a mage working alone and a great deal to a faculty that has learned to read it together.

effects.gloss: Once a shared registry of names is legible to the whole faculty, study of them never falls below this pace.
The same open ledger, once understood, also steadies how fast a name's holder can be taught to use it.

name: Refuse the Name's End
gloss: A name argued out of its own ending. Not immortality — a refusal, renewed, of the specific decline a held name would otherwise suffer.

effects.gloss: A floor under how reliably the named thing arrives, whatever grounds it might otherwise have claimed.
Once it is understood how a held name decays, refusing that decay is worth a century, guaranteed — but only once the decay itself has been made legible to refuse.

name: The Name That Outlasts
gloss: The deepest reading of the open-ledger doctrine, turned toward its holder rather than her students: a name kept so completely that it outlasts the ordinary span of the woman who kept it.

effects.gloss: Two hundred years guaranteed against decline, and a hard cap at four hundred: the working extends a life, it does not abolish the idea of one, and it can never exceed what a mage's own species base permits.
A faculty led by a mage who has outlasted her own decline studies no slower than this, for as long as she is there to lead it.

name: Set the Stone
gloss: Put a block exactly where it belongs, on the first attempt, without a crane.

effects.gloss: A floor under construction: the crews may be short-handed, but the work never stalls below this rate.

name: Mark the Quarry Empty
gloss: Declare a seam spent and leave it, on principle, before it is actually exhausted.

effects.gloss: A hard cap on what this one quarry will ever give up again, deliberately imposed.

name: Raise the Course
gloss: Lay a whole course of a wall as one working. Vision §4's worked example: earth magic building universities faster is a number here, not a special case in code.

effects.gloss: A deeper construction floor, bought by a mage who has decided the work goes on regardless.

name: Leave the Seam Unopened
gloss: Refuse a quarry that every other mason would have already opened, and mean it.

effects.gloss: A hard cap on this refusal's own yield: the point is what is left in the ground, not what comes out of it.

name: Quarry Without Hands
gloss: Compel stone out of a seam that no crew could reach and down to where it is wanted.

effects.gloss: A floor under what the seam gives up, whatever the crew's skill.
Once the seam's full extent is legible, the stone it yields also steadies the pace of the works it feeds.

name: The Fallow Doctrine
gloss: The formal practice of leaving ground alone. Worth nothing to a mage who has cut a single stone; the whole of it is refusal.

effects.gloss: Once the doctrine's discipline is legible, a seam left unopened recovers its yield no slower than this. The fallow ground pays, eventually, for having been left alone.
Fallow ground defends itself, once that is understood — but only up to a cap, since nothing has been raised to reinforce it further.

name: The Vaulted Hall
gloss: Hold a span up while it is built, so that it can be built at a size that could not have stood while unfinished. Every great library in the subset is one of these.

effects.gloss: A guaranteed pace of construction, and a hard cap on it too: no vault rises faster than its own vaulting allows.
Two great halls under construction at once draw on the quarries harder than either alone.

name: The Endless Course
gloss: A wall that is never finished because it is never allowed to stop being laid.

effects.gloss: The floor under a construction effort large enough to never fully complete.
The quarries feeding an endless course never drop below this, or the course stops, and it may not stop.

name: The Unquarried Mind
gloss: Leave the ground exactly as long as everyone else needed it built, and the ground holds for you in a way it holds for no one who has quarried it. Reachable only by refusing quarry-without-hands and its whole line.

effects.gloss: Land that has never been cut defends itself more reliably than any built wall, and no better than this — the doctrine does not build, it only holds.

name: Hold the Shadow Still
gloss: Compel a shadow to stay where it was cast while the thing that cast it moves. Nobody watches a shadow; they watch what it says is standing there.

name: The Lent Shadow
gloss: Put your shadow somewhere you are not and leave it there working. It is a poor likeness and an excellent alibi, and it holds for exactly as long as nobody speaks to it.

name: Step by Shadow
gloss: Enter one darkness and leave another in a single stride. It wants a shadow at both ends, which is why the wardens of careful universities keep the courtyards lit all night.

name: The Held Dark
gloss: Hold the dark of a place still and full until it stops being an absence and starts being something standing in the room. Everyone inside is hidden from everyone else, which favours whoever knew that going in.

name: Steady the Working
gloss: Hold a half-formed working still while you finish it. Most failed research is not wrong, merely interrupted, and this is the working that stops the interruption from counting.

name: Turn the Casting
gloss: Put your will between a working and the thing it was aimed at. The oldest defensive result in the literature, and still the one that decides duels between people who both have it.

name: The Working Kept in Iron
gloss: Bind a working into a thing, so that it goes on being cast without being cast again. Every well-appointed laboratory in the subset is a shelf of these, and every one of them was somebody's thesis.

name: Forbid the Casting
gloss: Bind the air of a place against workings that are not yours. Argument continues inside it; magic does not, and the distinction is enforced by the room rather than by anybody standing in it.

name: The Standing Prohibition
gloss: Hold a place against a whole body of magic indefinitely, without a god's edict and without a god's leave. A scholar who has one has written a ruling nobody signed; universities that keep one do not advertise it, and universities that have lost one write about very little else.
